In the reach from Maverick Dam to Eagle Pass, the average increase in flow levels between a 0 cfs release at Amistad and the expected 9,000 cfs release is less than 5 feet, which also varies at different locations. Below Eagle Pass, the flow levels should not fluctuate more than 3 feet between the 0 cfs release at Amistad and the expected 9,000 cfs release.
4.54 This increased rate of flow in the Rio Grande would not produce any new impact on fish and wildlife resources. The same beneficial and adverse impacts would arise, and the magnitude of the net effects should be very similar to those produced by the 4,000 cfs release. Only the length of time should vary since the increased rate of flow would produce similar effects in a shorter amount of time.
4.55 The combined releases would increase the rate of bank sloughing initially, which would likewise affect vegetational resources located along the banks of the Rio Grande.
4.56 Construction activities on the Mexican side should produce essentially the same impacts as discussed for the US side.
